chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Joining Don Redman in June 1932 and the band's lineup
summary: He took Fred Robinson's place on June 6, 1932; Jackson lists the whole band including Horace Henderson, with CBS broadcasts from Connie's Inn.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, we were just talking, to continue what we were doing last week, we were talking about Don Redmon and his arrangements and we were talking about some of the instrumentalists.
Now what do you remember, Butter, about -- Did we talk about Seventh Avenue and what it was like and the rhythm club?
Seventh Avenue was a boulevard, a beautiful boulevard when I first came to New York.
I came to New York in May 1932. I joined Don Redmon June 6, 1932. I took Fred Robinson's place.
Yeah. And a beautiful experience I'll never forget as long as I live because to me there was no band that sounded like that.
Who was in that band, Butter?
Well, the trumpets was Langston Curl and Shirley Clay --

Yeah.-- and Sidney DeParis. Now, Shirley Clay, he got him from Earl Hines. And the trombones was Claude Jones and Bennie Morton and myself. And the saxophones was Rupert Cole and Edward Inge and Bob Carroll and, of course, Don himself. And Horace Henderson was on piano.
That's right. Manzie Johnson was the drummer and Talcott Reeves was the guitar player.
What a beautiful band. We used to broadcast over CBS three times a week and then every night we used to broadcast over [WMC.]
